text: For centuries, sailors told a story nobody believed.
At night, the whole sea turned white. Glowing, like a field of snow.
For a long time, it sounded like folklore.
In 2019, a satellite caught a patch of glowing ocean south of Java.
About a hundred thousand square kilometers. Roughly the size of Iceland.
And it kept glowing for weeks.
By pure chance, a sailing yacht crossed right through it.
The crew said the water was brighter than the night sky.
The prime suspect: bacteria. Trillions upon trillions, glowing together once there are enough of them.
But why there? Why then? What sets it off? Scientists still don't know.
